triage.verifier_notes: Two caveats for the reviewer. (1) The first reader's narrative detail overstates what the parent actually computed: at the parent commit `tools/b16_entry_flags.py` defines `entry_is_line_a..e` as exact per-line identity (`hts == "7202111000"` etc.), so the pre-fix §122 gate zeroed the surcharge only on those two exemplar lines, not literally "on all Section 301-listed lines for every origin." The PR's "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" is the coupling hazard under the membership semantics the generalization requires (one flag cannot mean both "§122 (aa)(ii) exempt" and "China-301 list-1 member"). The scope defect is real under either reading — with identity flags the chapter's own §301/§232/§201 components could never fire on any chapter-63 line while Brazil/forced-labor fired on all of them — so the kind holds even though the quoted mechanism is the counterfactual one. (2) Runner-up kind is untraceable_branch: the pre-fix conditions are witness exemplar-line artifacts with no chapter-63 source basis and the fix "re-grounds" them. I kept wrong_entity_or_scope because the branch structure itself (a §122 exception for excluded and §232-covered articles) is in the cited source; only the population predicate was wrong. Also note the same diff adds `ch63_s232_steel_heading_rate` / `section_232_steel_component_rate` and wires it into the stack — per the PR that is new coverage the witness never had (its steel exemplar is a ferroalloy outside note 16(c)), so it is enhancement rather than the defect, and should not be counted as a second finding on this module. Last, the retained §122 proof-atom excerpt for `chapter-99/page-230` does not appear in the pinned corpus text at that path (Rev 3 page-230 is §232 steel TRQ notes), but that provenance mismatch is unchanged by this commit and is outside the candidate.
